skill.name: dast-nuclei
skill.description: Guides authorized Nuclei DAST scanning for web applications, APIs, and infrastructure. It covers target scoping, template selection, authentication patterns, CI workflows, and finding review.
skill.summary: Plan and run authorized Nuclei vulnerability scans with practical templates and review guidance.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation examples, placeholders, or expected Nuclei scanning guidance and were dismissed as false positives. One critical issue remains: a CI template installs tfsec with a remote curl-to-bash pipeline. Additional risks include mutable GitHub Action references and sensitive data handling in authenticated scans and extractors.

remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-bash with a pinned release, checksum verification, or a trusted package manager installation step.
Pin third-party GitHub Actions to immutable commit SHAs and review updates through normal dependency management.
Redact sensitive evidence, reduce artifact retention, and restrict artifact access for authenticated scan results.
Prefer presence-based evidence or masked extractors instead of storing full API keys, tokens, database URLs, or secrets.
Require explicit target allowlists, written authorization, conservative rate limits, and production exclusions in reusable workflows.

semantic_findings.description: The workflow template uses projectdiscovery/nuclei-action@main. A mutable branch can change CI behavior without review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow directly references a third-party action on the main branch. This is a clear supply-chain risk in CI templates.

semantic_findings.title: Authenticated Scan Artifacts May Expose Sensitive Data
semantic_findings.description: The authenticated scan uses API tokens and session cookies, then uploads raw results as an artifact. Results can contain sensitive URLs or response evidence.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file shows secrets passed as scan headers and authenticated results uploaded with retention. Nuclei output may not include headers, so confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Value Extraction Requires Guardrails
semantic_findings.description: Example templates extract API keys, database URLs, JWT secrets, and exposed configuration values from target responses. Reports should record evidence without storing secret values.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The templates intentionally match and extract sensitive values from HTTP responses. This is legitimate DAST behavior, but it creates data-handling risk if outputs are retained or shared.

content.value_statement: Manual vulnerability checks miss known CVEs and configuration issues across web apps and APIs. This skill helps plan Nuclei scans, tune CI workflows, and review findings.
actual_capabilities: Guides target scoping, template selection, severity filtering, and rate limits for Nuclei scans.
Provides GitHub Actions and CI configuration examples for automated vulnerability scanning.
Documents authenticated scanning with bearer tokens, sessions, OAuth, SAML, and MFA examples.
Shows custom Nuclei template patterns for CVEs, misconfigurations, and exposed data checks.
Explains false positive review, OWASP mapping, CWE mapping, and report preparation.
limitations: It does not grant permission to scan third-party systems.
It requires Nuclei and current templates to be installed separately.
Scan findings need manual validation before creating incidents.
Authenticated scans can expose sensitive result data if artifacts are shared.

use_cases.title: Validate Release Candidates
use_cases.description: Run focused Nuclei checks against staging services before release gates.

use_cases.title: Automate CI Security Checks
use_cases.description: Add severity-based Nuclei scans and artifact reporting to GitHub Actions.

use_cases.title: Build Custom Detection Templates
use_cases.description: Create organization-specific templates for exposed configs, weak auth, and known CVEs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner scoping for one authorized target.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a conservative Nuclei scan for one staging web app. Include scope, severity, rate limits, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Scan Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me triage these Nuclei findings. Group by severity, identify likely false positives, and suggest manual verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a CI Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GitHub Actions workflow for authorized Nuclei scanning. Use high severity gates, safe artifact handling, and clear failure behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Authenticated Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an authenticated Nuclei testing plan for APIs with bearer tokens and sessions. Include secret handling, exclusions, and reporting controls.

output_examples.input: I need a first scan plan for a staging web app.
output: A scoped scan plan with allowed targets, excluded endpoints, selected severities, and rate limits.
A validation checklist for critical and high findings before escalation.
A short report outline for security and engineering teams.

output_examples.input: I want Nuclei in CI without blocking every build.
output: A workflow design that runs on pull requests, scheduled jobs, and manual dispatch.
A severity gate that blocks only confirmed critical findings.
Artifact and notification guidance that avoids exposing sensitive scan data.

output_examples.input: I need a custom template for exposed application configuration.
output: A template design with target paths, safe matchers, and evidence-focused extractors.
Review steps for reducing false positives and avoiding storage of secret values.

best_practices: Obtain written authorization and define target scope before any scan.
Use conservative rate limits on production systems and validate high impact findings manually.
Redact tokens, cookies, and sensitive response data before sharing reports.
anti_patterns: Do not scan third-party systems without explicit permission.
Do not upload raw authenticated scan artifacts to broad-access locations.
Do not rely on template results without manual verification for critical findings.

faq.question: Does this skill run scans by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides Nuclei usage and provides templates. The user or CI environment runs Nuclei.

faq.question: Is authorization required before scanning?
faq.answer: Yes. Only scan systems where you have explicit permission and a defined scope.

faq.question: Can it support authenticated scans?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents token, cookie, OAuth, SAML, and MFA patterns for authorized testing.

faq.question: Can it help with false positives?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes review guidance for verifying findings and mapping them to OWASP and CWE.

faq.question: Does it replace a full penetration test?
faq.answer: No. Nuclei automates known checks, but manual testing is still needed for business logic issues.

faq.question: What should be protected in reports?
faq.answer: Protect target URLs, request details, tokens, cookies, screenshots, and response data from authenticated scans.
